item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Had my aeronautics engineer boyfriend poke at the numbers on this, ignoring factors like atmospheric drag. At first, it seemed promising- the force described is enough to lift the mentioned tank about 200 feet directly against one Earth gravity within the relevant 30 seconds, which is a more meaningful statement than simply "lift".

Then he decided to do the math for the actual 10kg hand dryer. In the first second, it would exceed escape velocity for Earth's gravity well. Assuming it didn't hit anything big enough to stop it, as of the end of its 30-second unpowered period, it would be going roughly 1/138th the speed of light. That means that in 30 seconds, it would be going over 100 times as fast as the top speed of the Voyager 1, the fastest thing humans have ever made.

+ show block
– hide block

This thing needs a serious nerf. I thought I would just add some missing description, but the current numbers are waaaay out of the range to cause the described effects. This thing should have blasted itself well out of the solar system the first time it activated, not ended up in a cycle where it can be re-installed. Even if it hit the ground, it would just skip and eventually tumble until it pointed up, up and away.

He just keeps coming up with ever more horrific implications. Like: mount this on one spot with a solid enough mounting and point it either normal or antinormal (the direction of Earth's spin or against it), and you can de-orbit the Earth, either in the direction of the sun or out of the Solar system. Put it at the north or south poles, and you can change the tilt axis of the Earth.

Oh, and if it's moving freely, it would be creating the nuclear explosion equivalent of sonic booms as it passes through the atmosphere. From what he's telling me, this would literally have caused the nuclear extinction of all life if it fired off horizontally, as implied in the description.

I do get that it was written a long time ago, but it looked like it had gotten some updates, including the addendum, much more recently. I suspect whoever did the addendum, like me, thought that just clearing things up a bit would help, but this needs a serious numbers adjustment to make the effects work as described.

My boyfriend seems interested now; would it be useful/okay if I had him recrunch for the desired effects and adjusted the numbers?

item.title: -1'd
item.content:encoded:
The idea is nice1, but it could be expressed in a more formal/scientific way. For instance, instead of "it is indestructible", a better form could be "proved to be indestructible to all means currently available to the Foundation, as well as invulnerable to its own properties", or something like that –if there's something powerful enough to destroy the entirety of Reality (and there is, see 2312), then it's likely also able to destroy 313, thus proving its non-indestructability. You get the idea.

TL;DR: Overall it's not an awful article, and maybe I'm just a bloody nitpicker, but I think it needs a complete re-write for tone and wording.

Footnotes
1. Nothing TERRIFICLY GNARLY AWESOME ZOMG, but still "would-be-a-fun-read"-nice.
2. …I guess…

"first and foremost, it is utterly indestructible and impervious to all forces available to us, and secondly, it is extraordinarily destructive, apparently by design."
